item.title: Stay a Little While Longer
item.description: My granny went on hospice this week. My granny, who helped raise my sister and me. The sweetest and most loving woman you could ever know. She is 90 now, and we all know it is such a blessing that she was here for so long. Many people don’t have their granny well into their 30s. item.title: If I Can Do It, You Can Do It: Get the Colonoscopy
item.description: I have a crappy stomach. (In a moment, you will really appreciate that pun.) For years, foods have caused discomfort. item.description: There’s something special about blogger kids. The ones raised in front of a camera lens, the ones finding a voice for themselves before they had the chance to speak. item.title: What the Difficult Person on Your Christmas List Really Wants
item.description: We’ve all got one on our Christmas list. The difficult person to shop for, or the person who could have everything. But if I could tell you the truth about so many of us…you might be surprised to know the gift we love the most. We don’t want a gift because it’s expected. Truth is, we’d rather not have a physical gift at all unless it’s something we use regularly or keep on a wishlist for one day. You can give it to us, but there’s a good chance it’ll be donated if we don’t need it or it doesn’t.

item.title: Love, Long after the Vows
item.description: When we pulled into the parking lot of one of our traditional vacation restaurants this year, the lot was unexpectedly empty for a Saturday night. “Uh, oh!” John said. “Looks like this one may be in trouble too.” Our local restaurant with the same name burned over a year ago, and wasn’t rebuilt, and I was looking forward to our yearly vacation visit even more than usual. We walked in, and the restaurant was nearly empty. It took a bit for someone to acknowledge us and lead us to a nearby booth.

item.title: To the Moms Who Love Quiet
item.description: I’ve always been the quiet one. The listener. The observer. The one who never minded silence and didn’t feel the need to fill it. Even as an adult, that part of me never changed. item.description: I might have missed my son’s last Christmas with Santa. I was there, and I watched it happen, but it never occurred to me that it might be his last.
